[[File:Euphorbia hirta NP.JPG|thumb|right|Euphorbia hirta in [[Panchkhal]] valley]]
'''''Euphorbia hirta''''' (sometimes called '''asthma-plant'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref>) is a [[pantropical]] weed, originating from the tropical regions of the Americas.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Royal Botanic Garden Sydney PlantNET Database Entry |publisher=Royal Botanical Gardens Sydney |url=https://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&showsyn=&dist=&constat=&lvl=sp&name=Euphorbia~hirta |access-date=2021-01-23 }}</ref> It is a hairy herb that grows in open [[grassland]]s, roadsides and pathways. It is widely used in traditional [[herbal medicine]] across many cultures, particularly for [[asthma]], skin ailments, and [[hypertension]].<ref name=Kumar>{{cite journal |vauthors=Kumar S, Malhotra R, Kumar D |year=2010 |title=''Euphorbia hirta'': Its chemistry, traditional and medicinal uses, and pharmacological activities |journal=Pharmacognosy Reviews  |volume=4 |issue=7 |pages=58–61 |doi= 10.4103/0973-7847.65327|pmid= 22228942|pmc= 3249903 |doi-access=free }}</ref> It is also consumed in [[herbal tea]] form as folk medicine for fevers in the [[Philippines]] (where it is known as '''tawa-tawa'''), particularly for [[dengue fever]] and [[malaria]].<ref name="Yam">{{cite journal |last1=Yam |first1=Hilton Y. |last2=Montaño |first2=Marco Nemesio E. |last3=Sia |first3=Isidro C. |last4=Heralde |first4=Francisco M. III |last5=Tayao |first5=Lotgarda |title=Ethnomedicinal Uses of tawatawa (Euphorbia hirta Linn.) in Selected Communities in the Philippines: a Non-invasive Ethnographic Survey Using Pictures for Plant Identification |journal=Acta Medica Philippina |date=2018 |volume=52 |issue=5 |doi=10.47895/amp.v52i5.325 |url=https://actamedicaphilippina.upm.edu.ph/index.php/acta/article/view/325|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title='Tawa-tawa': Herbal supplement that can help fight dengue |url=https://www.philstar.com/lifestyle/health-and-family/2019/10/08/1957088/tawa-tawa-herbal-supplement-can-help-fight-dengue |access-date=7 September 2021 |work=PhilStar Global |date=8 October 2019}}</ref>

==Description==

This erect or prostrate [[Annual plant|annual herb]] can grow up to {{convert|60|cm|abbr=on}} long with a solid stem that is furnished with many yellow to reddish coarse hairs, and produces an abundant white latex.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.oswaldasia.org/species/e/euphi/euphi_en.html |title=Open Source for Weed Assessment in Lowland Paddy Fields (OSWALD) |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=2007-07-21 |publisher=Asia IT&C Programme of the European Union |access-date=August 30, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130709143931/http://www.oswaldasia.org/species/e/euphi/euphi_en.html |archive-date=July 9, 2013  }}</ref> There are [[stipules]] present. The leaves have an oblique base and are [[Simple leaf|simple]], elliptical to slightly rhombic, hairy (on both upper and lower surfaces but particularly on the veins on the lower leaf surface), with a finely dentate margin, the veins upperside being deep-set and conspicuous on the underside, and the leaf surface somewhat leathery. Leaves occur in opposite pairs on the stem. The flowers are [[unisexual]] and found in axillary [[cymes]] at each leaf node, held as dense balls of flowers and fruit capsules usually close to the stem, the flower glands with tiny white/pinkish petal-like appendages. The fruit is a capsule with three valves (creating 3 sides), uniformly appressed hairy, containing tiny (0.7–0.9 mm), oblong, four-sided orange to pink or red seeds. It has a white or brown [[taproot]]. [http://floranorthamerica.org/Euphorbia_hirta FNA]

==Taxonomy==
''Euphorbia hirta'' was given its scientific name by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in 1753. It continues to be classified in the genus ''[[Euphorbia]]'' within the family [[ Euphorbiaceae]]. It has no accepted [[Variety (Botany)|varieties]], but has some among its {{table row counter|id=Synonyms}} [[Synonym (botany)|synonyms]].<ref name="POWO">{{cite POWO |id=101651-2 |title=''Euphorbia hirta'' L. |access-date=2 November 2025}}</ref>

===Names===
''Euphorbia hirta'' has many [[common name]]s including ''garden spurge'', ''pillpod spurge'', and ''hairy spurge''. It is also called by the related names ''asthma weed'', ''asthma plant'' and ''Queensland asthma weed''. Additionally it is known as ''red milkweed'' and ''snakeweed''.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Randall |first1=Roderick Peter |date=2002 |title=A global compendium of weeds |url=https://archive.org/details/globalcompendium0000rand |url-access=registration |location=Melbourne, Australia |publisher=R.G. and F.J. Richardson |page=192 |isbn=978-0-9587439-8-3 |oclc=50867942 |access-date=2 November 2025}}</ref>
